ENGINEERING EXPERIENCE
Bloom Energy (Newark, DE) - Repair & Overhaul / Engineering Intern Jun 2026 - Aug 2026
IRIS — Integrated Reliability Imaging System
● Designed and engineered Bloom's first machine vision inspection system for returned fuel cell columns, capturing burns and field
damage before teardown, enabling computer vision model training and data-driven operating decisions that extend unit lifespan.
● Derived the optical specification from a 0.1 mm feature-resolution requirement to 53 μm/px across the full column face (5 MP
sensor, 35 mm lens, ±13 mm depth-of-field standoff window); verified zero-gap five-camera coverage by script and rejected
motorized single-camera alternative on cycle time and drift.
● Owned optical requirements, mechanical design, capture software, procurement, V&V, and handoff to operations; concept to
handoff in 8 weeks, with no change to the existing teardown workflow and no contact with production tooling.
● Built automated focus and exposure acceptance gates into the capture software (~2k LOC; Python, FastAPI), with operator
overrides logged to per-unit metadata so every accepted image carries its own acceptance evidence.
● Delivered a seven-document operations handoff: commissioning runbook, design decision log, V&V record with open items
tracked to closure, code guide for non-programmers, and asset inventory.
Mujin (Atlanta, GA) - Product Development Intern Jan 2026 - Apr 2026
EOAT Vacuum Cup Validation • Fleet Reliability Monitoring
● Authored a two-phase supplier-change validation plan qualifying a replacement vacuum cup on a 63-cup depalletizing gripper,
with adopt / reject / limited-deployment decision logic, must-not-worsen acceptance criteria, and metrics per 10,000 picks.
● Ran Phase 1 bench testing on a force/vacuum jig with KEYENCE digital pressure sensing: pull-off force, 10-second static
retention, and vacuum decay across a 2–10 lb load range and five surface conditions, against a ≤10% decay acceptance gate.
● Structured Phase 2 as a 30/60/90-day A/B field comparison on a live production line, stratified by weight and surface type, with a
failure mode framework supporting the go/no-go decision; led field testing at a 24/7 customer distribution center.
● The plan’s field phase caught a durability failure that bench testing missed: replacement cups cracked and wore within about two
weeks, and the pre-set criteria called a no-swap before any fleet-wide rollout; two new metrics were added to fleet monitoring.
● Built StatsMonitor (~5.8k LOC Python), a fleet reliability pipeline covering 13 controllers at 6 customer sites whose
evidence-gated daily KPI report and ranked watchlist the service team uses to decide which units get attention first.
BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH
Sulchek Lab, Georgia Tech (Atlanta, GA) - Undergraduate Researcher Jun 2025 - Present
AFM Measurement & Damage Characterization
● Owned the damage analysis for a 397-indentation AFM dataset (102 naive T cells across four post-thaw days), with report
numbers regenerated from scripts and a regression baseline that must reproduce after every change.
● Showed that achieved (not commanded) indentation load and rate account for several times more modulus variance than
measurement day; built the harmonization pipeline to carry achieved values as covariates rather than assume setpoints.
● Built cell-detection pipeline (85-frame series averaging, fixed-pattern dust subtraction, and per-session cantilever drift registration
lifting one day’s target detection from 62% to 96%), delivered 31,000+ target/bystander cell crops to lab's downstream pipeline.
